chapter.v:
Don't boast
about what you're going to do tomorrow, because you don't know what the day may bring.

Let others
praise you, not you yourself; someone else, not you personally.

Stone may
be heavy, and sand may weigh a lot, but the annoyance caused by stupid people is the biggest burden of all.

Fury may
be fierce and cruel, anger may be a destructive flood, but who can withstand jealousy?

Open criticism
is better than hidden love.

A friend's
honest comments may hurt you, but an enemy's kisses are over the top.

If you're
full up, you can't face honey; but if you're starving, even bitter food tastes sweet.

Having to
leave home is like a bird having to leave its nest.

Perfume and
scented oils make you feel happy, but good advice from a friend is even better.

Don't give
up on your friends or your family's friends. Don't go to a relative's house when you've got trouble. A friend nearby is more useful than a relative far away.

My son,
make me happy by being wise, so I can respond to anyone who criticizes me.

If you're
sensible you see danger coming and get out of the way; but stupid people just keep going and suffer the consequences.

If someone
guarantees a stranger's debt with their cloak, be sure to take it! Make sure you have whatever is pledged to an immoral woman!

If when
you get up every morning you shout a loud hello to your neighbors, they will see that as a curse!

An argumentative
wife is as irritating as constant dripping on a rainy day.

Trying to
stop her is like trying to make the wind stop or trying to hold olive oil in your hand.

An iron
blade is sharpened with an iron tool, and one person's mind is sharpened by another's.

Those who
care for a fig tree eat its fruit, and those who care for their master are rewarded.

Just as
water reflects your face, your mind reflects who you really are.

In the
same way that the grave and destruction are never satisfied, human desire is never satisfied.

Just as
a crucible tests silver, and a furnace tests gold, people are tested by the praise they receive.

Even if
you ground stupid people in a mortar, crushing them like grain with the pestle, you can't get rid of stupidity from them.

You should
know the condition of your flocks really well and take good care of your herds,

for wealth
doesn't last forever—is a crown passed down through all generations?

Once the
hay is cut, and the new growth begins, and fodder from the mountains is gathered,

and the
lambs have provided you wool to make clothing, and the sale of goats have paid for a field,

there'll be
enough milk from your goats to feed you, your family, and your servant girls.
